question: Assuming Gareth Evan's Generality Constraint, if I understand a proposition Fa, should I be able to understand Fx (\forall x)? Assume I understand universal quantification.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Yes. Evans' Generality Constraint requires that if a thinker grasps the thought Fa (i.e., possesses the constituent concepts a and F), then they must be able to recombine those constituents with any other appropriate concepts they possess. Given the additional assumption that the thinker already grasps universal quantification, this recombination immediately licenses the thought ∀x Fx. The constraint rules out any "local" or non-general understanding of F that would block this move. 

(The answer is therefore affirmative under the stated assumptions.)

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Yes, under Evans' Generality Constraint, grasp of Fa should enable grasp of ∀x Fx once universal quantification is independently understood. The constraint requires that any thinker who possesses the predicative concept F and can apply it to one object a must be able to apply it to any other object they can single out; universal quantification simply collects all such possible applications into a single thought. Because the constraint is precisely what guarantees that F remains the same concept across different singular positions, and because we are assuming the quantifier itself is mastered, nothing further blocks the thinker from forming the universally quantified thought. This recombinability is what distinguishes structured thought from merely atomic representations, so the transition from Fa to ∀x Fx follows directly.

Given the further assumption that the subject already grasps the universal quantifier, this recombinability immediately yields grasp of ∀x Fx.

This preserves the systematicity Evans emphasizes without requiring any additional non-compositional capacity.

Because the constraint demands recombinability of the constituent concepts (the singular term and the predicate), one can substitute variables for the understood singular term while holding F fixed. Given independent mastery of universal quantification, this recombination directly yields understanding of ∀x Fx: the quantifier simply binds the open position made available by the recombinable structure. No further conceptual resources are required beyond what the Constraint already supplies.

Given independent grasp of the universal quantifier, this recombinatorial capacity immediately yields understanding of ∀x Fx. The constraint is precisely what licenses the move from an atomic instance to the fully general quantified proposition.

(The constraint does not, of course, guarantee that the quantified proposition is true, only that it is intelligible once Fa is grasped.)

The two abilities remain independent even when the quantifier itself is understood.

(The constraint is silent on whether the domain of quantification coincides with the range of singular thoughts one can form.)
